entries.sense_en: alone, without help from anyone else

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for being by yourself; single-handed stresses doing a hard task with no help.
More formal; often used for achievements or seeing without tools (the unaided eye).
Informal or technical; common for flights, music and sports performances.

entries.sense_en: in British India, a permanent area where soldiers and officials lived
entries.sense_ko: (영국령 인도의) 군 주둔지, 영국인 거주 구역

synonyms.nuance: Modern everyday word for a military station; cantonment is historical, tied to colonial India.
Usually temporary tents or huts; a cantonment was a permanent town-like settlement.
Focuses on the troops stationed in a town to defend it, or the fort itself.

entries.sense_en: ran with short, quick steps, like a small animal

synonyms.nuance: Very close; scurry adds a sense of hurry or panic.
Playful, light running, often of children or small animals.
synonyms.example: The puppies scampered around the yard.

synonyms.nuance: One sudden fast run to a place; no idea of small, quick steps.

entries.sense_en: a hole or tunnel in the ground where a small animal lives

synonyms.nuance: Home of a larger wild animal like a fox or bear; not necessarily dug.
General word for any opening; burrow says an animal dug it and lives in it.
A hiding place of a dangerous animal, or figuratively of a villain.

entries.tip_ko: borrow(빌리다)와 철자·발음이 비슷하니 주의: burrow /ˈbɝoʊ/, borrow /ˈbɑroʊ/.

entries.sense_en: a small, thin bunch of grass, hair or smoke

synonyms.nuance: One single thread or hair; a wisp is a light, loose little bunch.
A bunch growing or fixed together at the base, like grass or feathers.
A small torn piece; often used for 'not a shred of evidence'.

entries.sense_en: wet, dirty and messy, as if dragged through mud

synonyms.nuance: The common modern form with the same meaning.
synonyms.example: a bedraggled cat after the rain

synonyms.nuance: Only says very wet; draggled adds dirty and untidy.
Untidy hair or clothes, not necessarily wet or muddy.

entries.sense_en: completely filled with a strong feeling

synonyms.nuance: More formal; usually negative feelings like guilt or jealousy.
Neutral and weak; eaten up with suggests the feeling controls you.
Positive, lively feelings that almost spill out.

entries.sense_en: smelled something by breathing in noisily through the nose

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word; snuff in this sense is old-fashioned.
General verb; does not describe short, noisy breaths.
Repeated noisy sniffing, as with a cold or an animal searching.

entries.sense_en: moving around a place freely, with no fixed plan

synonyms.nuance: Slower, more aimless, sometimes getting lost; roam suggests freedom over a wide area.
Has a purpose: to learn about a new place.
A long relaxed walk in the countryside; also talking too long.

entries.sense_en: raised by parents to behave politely and correctly

synonyms.nuance: Older, suggests good family and upper-class manners; also used for animals.
synonyms.example: Rikki-tikki was too well bred to bite.

synonyms.nuance: Only about present behavior, not upbringing.
Everyday word for courteous behavior in one situation.

entries.sense_en: met or found by chance

synonyms.nuance: Informal; usually meeting a person you know unexpectedly.
synonyms.example: I ran into my teacher at the mall.

synonyms.nuance: More formal; often used for problems or difficulties.
Finding something lucky or interesting completely by accident.

entries.sense_en: areas where bushes or plants grow very close together

synonyms.nuance: One single plant; a thicket is many growing densely together.
Low plants covering the ground under trees in a forest.
British; a small group of trees, not bushes.

entries.sense_en: soft and fluffy, like the very small feathers of a young bird

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; soft and light with lots of air, like a towel or cloud.
Covered with short, soft hairs; also means unclear.
Light and delicate in shape, like a feather.

entries.sense_en: first one way and then the other, again and again

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern phrase; to and fro sounds literary.
Clearly left–right movement, like a swinging head or ship.
synonyms.example: The boat rocked from side to side.

synonyms.nuance: Vertical movement, or walking along a place and back.

entries.sense_en: bent low and stayed still because they were afraid

synonyms.nuance: Bending low for any reason (hiding, sport); cower always means fear.
A quick pulling back in fear, or today mostly in embarrassment.
synonyms.example: I cringe when I hear my old songs.

synonyms.nuance: Crowding close together, often for warmth or comfort.

entries.sense_en: young birds that have just grown feathers and are learning to fly

synonyms.nuance: Any baby bird, especially a newly hatched one or a young chicken.
A baby bird still too young to leave the nest.
Figurative use of fledgling: a beginner in a field.

entries.sense_en: not ready or watchful, so easy to attack or surprise

synonyms.nuance: The most common modern form: surprised when you were not ready.
synonyms.example: The question caught me off guard.

synonyms.nuance: Literary; 'take someone unawares' means surprise them.
Plain word; about lacking preparation, not attention in the moment.

entries.sense_en: was wise enough not to do something

synonyms.nuance: Informal and direct; know better stresses experience or training.
synonyms.example: He's too smart to fall for that.

synonyms.nuance: Simpler; just says you have learned a rule.
synonyms.example: Kids know not to touch the stove.

synonyms.nuance: A criticism: someone did a foolish thing they ought to avoid.
synonyms.example: You should know better at your age.

entries.tip_ko: '더 잘 안다'로 직역하면 오역. '~하지 않을 분별이 있다'는 뜻.

entries.sense_en: moved past very fast, with a rushing sound

synonyms.nuance: Very fast movement, mostly of vehicles; less about the sound.
Stresses the soft rushing sound of air.
Moving by so quickly it is seen only for an instant.
synonyms.example: A bird flashed past the window.

entries.sense_en: twisted its body with small quick movements

synonyms.nuance: Twisting from discomfort, pain or embarrassment.
Strong, violent twisting, usually in great pain.
Lighter, often playful, small movements of a part of the body.

entries.sense_en: a particular way of walking or moving

synonyms.nuance: One long step, or a confident way of walking with long steps.
Speed of walking, not its style.
Everyday noun; gait is more technical, used by doctors and writers.
synonyms.example: I know him by his walk.

entries.sense_en: moved forward suddenly and forcefully to attack

synonyms.nuance: Jumping down on prey from above or from hiding.
synonyms.example: The cat pounced on the mouse.

synonyms.nuance: Pushing something (a sword, a hand) forward hard.
A sudden jump, not always forward or aggressive.

entries.sense_en: a lucky gift that seems sent by God to protect people
entries.sense_ko: 하늘이 보내 준 구원자, 신의 선물

synonyms.nuance: Modern everyday word for an unexpected, very helpful thing or person.
Anything good you are thankful for; weaker, less about rescue.
Informal; someone or something that helps a lot at the right moment.

entries.sense_en: eat until very full

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, a little medical; eating more than is healthy.
Eating greedily and a lot at once; stronger.
Very informal, humorous.

entries.sense_en: makes small, weak crying sounds

synonyms.nuance: A long high sound, or complaining in an annoying way.
Crying hard with short, loud breaths.
A long low sound of pain or unhappiness.

entries.sense_en: in a way that shows he thinks the idea is silly and not worth respect

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and colder; showing someone is worthless.
Making fun of someone, often by copying or laughing.
Treating something as unimportant, not always with open scorn.

entries.sense_en: a small opening or channel that lets water flow out

synonyms.nuance: The everyday modern word for a hole or pipe that takes water away.
A large gate controlling water in a river or canal.
Channel at a roof edge or roadside for rainwater.

entries.sense_en: moved away quietly and secretly

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; often suggests doing something not allowed.
Leaving quietly so nobody notices; no sense of danger.
synonyms.example: She slipped away from the party.

synonyms.nuance: Moving slowly and carefully, often close to the ground.

entries.sense_en: felt a slight stinging, prickling feeling on the skin because of strong emotion

synonyms.nuance: Like small sharp points on the skin; often from fear.
synonyms.example: The hair on my neck prickled.

synonyms.nuance: A sudden wave of excitement or pleasure.
Shaking slightly from cold or fear.

entries.match: the odds are in his favor
entries.sense_en: he is more likely to win

synonyms.nuance: A small advantage over a rival.
Already in control in a fight or argument.
synonyms.example: The police now have the upper hand.

synonyms.nuance: Deliberately making it unfair (against someone).
synonyms.example: The odds are stacked against us.

entries.sense_en: the rounded part that sticks out

synonyms.nuance: Usually on the body, from injury or illness.
A small hard shape, on the body or in food.
Neutral shape word; no idea of pushing outward.

entries.sense_en: wild with anger and ready to attack violently

synonyms.nuance: Strong and aggressive, but can be positive (a fierce competitor).
Extremely violent and frightening; stronger than fierce.
Violent with a wish to hurt; also cruel words.

entries.sense_en: pressed his body firmly against something to stay steady

synonyms.nuance: Keeping something from shaking or falling; less effort implied.
Supporting something by leaning an object against it.
Figurative: preparing for something bad.

entries.sense_en: a firm hold or grip that stops you from slipping

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for a firm hold with hands or feet.
synonyms.example: These shoes have a good grip.

synonyms.nuance: A place to put your foot; figuratively a first secure position.
synonyms.example: gain a foothold in the market

synonyms.nuance: Force gained by using a lever; figuratively, power to influence.

entries.sense_en: hit hard again and again

synonyms.nuance: Heavy repeated blows, often with fists or waves.
General word for hitting many times.
Pushed and knocked about by wind or waves.

entries.sense_en: felt certain (that something would happen)

synonyms.nuance: Modern way to say you strongly believe something.
Today it means check or ensure, not believe.
synonyms.example: Make sure the door is locked.

synonyms.nuance: Believing something without questioning it.

entries.sense_en: burned slightly on the surface or tips

synonyms.nuance: Burning a surface enough to leave a brown mark.
synonyms.example: scorched the shirt with the iron

synonyms.nuance: Burning until black.
General word, any degree of damage.

entries.sense_en: imagined or believed, without good reason

synonyms.nuance: The normal word; fancy in this sense is literary or British.
synonyms.example: I imagined I heard a noise.

synonyms.nuance: Guessing something is probably true; calmer.
In British English today it often means 'want' or 'like'.

entries.sense_en: very brave, especially in a fight

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; valiant is more formal and heroic.
Brave in facing fear, often moral situations.
Brave in a way that deserves great admiration.

entries.sense_en: said when annoyed; 'forget about' something unimportant

synonyms.nuance: Polite way to say something does not matter.
Blunt modern way to dismiss something.
Old-fashioned mild curse, stronger than bother.

entries.sense_en: even a very small amount of good judgment

synonyms.nuance: Same idea, a more common modern version.
synonyms.example: Anyone with an ounce of sense would leave.

synonyms.nuance: Basic practical judgment everyone should have.
Same 'grain' pattern: a small bit of truth.
synonyms.example: There's a grain of truth in it.

entries.sense_en: silly and unable to think seriously

synonyms.nuance: Disorganized and forgetful rather than foolish.
Harsher: without intelligence or ideas.
Mild everyday word; can be affectionate.

entries.sense_en: moved her wings quickly and lightly, flying low and unsteadily

synonyms.nuance: Bigger, slower wing movements.
Flying quickly from place to place.
Staying in one place in the air.

entries.sense_en: something that makes a sad or bad situation feel a little better

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; also physical ease.
Literary; comfort in deep sadness.
A small prize for someone who did not win.

entries.sense_en: take revenge on someone for a past wrong

synonyms.nuance: Informal; paying back harm with harm.
Revenge for an old, specific wrong.
Plain, direct phrase.

entries.sense_en: in a clever way meant to trick or hide

synonyms.nuance: Neutral or positive; no idea of trickery.
Secretly and a bit dishonestly, often with a smile.
Clever at tricking people, usually negative.

entries.sense_en: soon; in a short time

synonyms.nuance: The everyday modern word for this meaning.
Slightly formal; common in announcements.
Today presently often means 'now', like currently.

entries.sense_en: all the young animals born or hatched together from one mother

synonyms.nuance: Young of mammals like dogs or cats born at one time.
A set of eggs laid at one time.
Formal; any children or young of a person or animal.

entries.match: on the spur of the minute
entries.headword: on the spur of the moment
entries.sense_en: suddenly, without planning

synonyms.nuance: Acting on sudden feeling, sometimes unwisely.

synonyms.word: off the top of my head
synonyms.nuance: Saying something without checking or thinking long.
synonyms.example: Off the top of my head, about fifty.

synonyms.nuance: Natural and unplanned, often positive.

entries.modern: on the spur of the moment
entries.tip_ko: 표준 관용구는 on the spur of the moment. 원문의 minute는 이를 살짝 바꾼 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: shook slightly and quickly

synonyms.nuance: Shaking from fear, cold or weakness; usually of people.
One strong shake, from disgust or fear.
Slow movement side to side, not shaking.

entries.sense_en: very sad, like grieving for someone who has died

synonyms.nuance: Literary; deep sadness, not always about death.
Dark and hopeless mood or weather.
Long, quiet, thoughtful sadness.

entries.sense_en: in the past, a person who walked through a town shouting out news

synonyms.nuance: Modern person who reads news or information on radio or TV.
Historical messenger of a king; also a sign of something coming.
Someone who spreads private news, often unkindly.
